profile.headline: I build ML, optimization, and experimentation systems that change how people move — and prove that they work.
hero: I'm a Ph.D. candidate at **Georgia Tech** (minor in Technology Commercialization) with **8 years of research experience** on how people make travel decisions and interact with emerging mobility systems. I work end to end: from raw sensor data and modeling to deployed software and rigorous causal evaluation.

Highlights: I designed and shipped **GT TranSACT**, a native **iOS and Android app with a Firebase backend** used by ~150 participants in a live field study; built **Transformer-based travel-mode detection** from second-by-second GPS; ran randomized experiments with **10,000+ U.S. participants**; and formulated **bi-level network optimization** that achieves a **~20% reduction in network emissions**.

I also build with **PyTorch, HuggingFace, LoRA, and RAG**, train **reinforcement learning** agents in SUMO, and have run human-factors studies on high-fidelity **autonomous vehicle driving simulators** with EEG, ECG, and eye tracking. My work has earned **two 2025 Best Paper Awards** and **$300K in USDOT funding** through proposals I developed, and I received **GT Create-X** and **Fusen Fund** support to commercialize carbon-emission tracking technology.

experience.place: Autonomous & Connected Transportation Lab, Georgia Tech
items: **Shipped a production mobile sensing platform:** designed and built GT TranSACT for iOS (SwiftUI) and Android (Jetpack Compose) with passive GPS sensing, trip collection, and personalized messaging, on a Firebase backend (Auth, Cloud Storage, analytics); deployed to **~150 participants**
**Ran a 12-week longitudinal field experiment** in Metro Atlanta to promote walking and transit, recruiting **1,100+ participants** with IRB-compliant data ingestion and engagement pipelines
**Built ML pipelines for human mobility:** trip segmentation, Transformer-based travel-mode detection (GeoLife + local ground truth), and automated data-quality checks on second-by-second GPS

**Solved large-scale network optimization:** formulated a bi-level network design problem with stochastic user equilibrium, developed an adjoint KKT sensitivity method for high-dimensional gradients, benchmarked against PSO, and achieved **~20% emissions reduction**
**Trained RL agents for personalized incentives:** DDPG coupled with the SUMO microscopic traffic simulator, with a multi-objective reward balancing travel time and incentive spend

**Led human-factors research on autonomous vehicles:** built a 1.6-mile digital twin of the Curiosity Lab AV test track; collected driving, eye-tracking, EEG, and ECG data from 57 participants; findings informed AV infrastructure deployed on the track

**Won funding:** developed and secured **$300K in USDOT funding** (3 proposals, 3 consecutive years) and contributed to a **$2.5M NSF Smart & Connected Communities** grant with the City of Peachtree Corners

publications.authors: Anne, V. S. R., Liu, Y., Kibria, M. G., Peeta, S., & Asensio, O. I.

projects.title: GT TranSACT — iOS & Android Mobile Sensing Platform
projects.summary: Native iOS and Android research app with a Firebase backend for passive GPS sensing, trip collection, and personalized behavioral interventions.
items: Native iOS (SwiftUI) and Android (Jetpack Compose) apps with shared navigation and intervention design.
Passive GPS sensing, trip collection, personalized messaging, and engagement features (badges, trip history).
Backend architecture on **Firebase** Authentication, Cloud Storage, and analytics, plus remote experiment configuration.
HERE SDK integration for multimodal routing, address search, and turn-by-turn navigation.
IRB-compliant data ingestion pipelines linking second-by-second GPS and usage events with survey data for causal analysis.
Built with an undergraduate team I mentored through the VIP ACT Lab course.
projects.details: TranSACT is the platform layer connecting app-based behavioral interventions, real-time route choices, Firebase experiment controls, and high-resolution mobility data.
projects.impact: Designed, built, and deployed end to end · ~150 active participants in a live field study

projects.title: Transformer-Based Travel Mode Detection from GPS
projects.summary: ML pipeline that segments raw smartphone GPS traces into trips and infers travel mode and mobility patterns.
items: Transformer-based architecture trained on the **GeoLife** dataset and adapted with **local ground-truth** trajectories.
Pipelines for trip segmentation, travel-mode inference, and mobility pattern recognition.
Automated quality checks that flag missing coverage, anomalous coordinates, and implausible trajectories.
Feeds directly into the field experiment's measurement of intervention effects.
projects.details: This project automates mobility analytics by classifying travel mode from high-resolution smartphone traces, replacing manual trip labeling.
projects.impact: Transfer from GeoLife to locally labeled trajectories · automated data-quality checks

projects.title: Bi-Level Network Optimization for Intervention Design
projects.summary: Large-scale optimization that allocates monetary and non-monetary interventions across a transportation network while accounting for how travelers respond.
items: Formulated a **bi-level network design problem** with stochastic user equilibrium and travel choice.
Modeled heterogeneous user behavior under monetary and non-monetary decision variables.
Developed an **adjoint KKT sensitivity method** for high-dimensional gradient computation.
Benchmarked against **Particle Swarm Optimization** over a 12,124-variable search space.
Incorporated health and environmental externalities of travel at network scale; optimal strategies cut emissions by ~20%.
projects.details: This project streamlines intervention allocation as a network-level design problem, linking behavioral response to emissions and congestion outcomes.
projects.impact: ~20% network-wide emissions reduction · adjoint KKT gradients for a 12,124-variable problem

projects.title: Reinforcement Learning for Personalized, Dynamic Incentives
projects.summary: DDPG agent coupled with the SUMO microscopic traffic simulator that decides when and how much to incentivize travelers in real time.
items: Built a simulator-based **DDPG** training environment coupling neural policies with SUMO.
Designed a **multi-objective reward** balancing network-wide travel time against incentive spend.
Modeled high-dimensional continuous states (link travel times) and actions (incentives), updated every 15 minutes.
Simulated closed-loop interactions among RL actions, route choice, vehicle trajectories, and congestion.
projects.details: This project treats intervention timing and intensity as a dynamic control problem under network uncertainty.
projects.impact: ~15% traffic efficiency gain and ~25% CO₂ reduction in numerical experiments

awards.title: TRB AEP35 Best Paper Award — 104th Annual Meeting of the Transportation Research Board
description: Our paper **"Effectiveness of Health and Environmental Information Provision in Promoting Sustainable Travel Modes"** received the Best Paper Award from the AEP35 committee at the 104th Annual Meeting of the Transportation Research Board, Washington, D.C., January 2025.

The study examines whether health and environmental information, including gamified feedback, can increase traveler engagement with walking, biking, and public transit. Results from a large-scale randomized experiment show meaningful shifts in stated mode preferences when benefits are made personally salient.

awards.title: SpatialConnect 2025 Best Paper Award — ACM SIGSPATIAL Workshop
awards.imageAlt: Research team receiving the SpatialConnect Best Paper Award at ACM SIGSPATIAL 2025
description: Our collaborative research, *"Joint Optimization of Transit Stops and Routes to Improve Access to Essential Community Destinations,"* was awarded Best Paper at the SpatialConnect 2025 Workshop on Spatial Intelligence for Smart and Connected Communities, co-located with ACM SIGSPATIAL.

This work introduces a location-aware optimization framework that jointly determines bus stop placement and route design to maximize access to key destinations—grocery stores, medical facilities, and employment hubs. Applied to the City of Peachtree Corners, Georgia, the model demonstrates how data-driven transit design can strengthen community-scale accessibility and equity in suburban contexts.
This recognition reflects the broader goal of my work: building optimization and decision-support tools that turn mobility data into better, more equitable planning decisions.
